title: Dose-dense AC → weekly paclitaxel

agents.name: Doxorubicin
agents.explanation: Doxorubicin interferes with enzymes and DNA processes needed for cell division. It can also affect heart muscle, so the team considers previous exposure and cardiac risk.
agents.watch: Report pain or burning at the infusion site immediately. New breathlessness or chest symptoms need prompt review. Red urine for a short time can be a drug-colour effect; pain, clots or persistent bleeding still need advice.
risks: Low counts, infection and mouth ulcers
Severe tissue injury if the infusion leaks

agents.name: Cyclophosphamide
agents.explanation: Cyclophosphamide is activated in the body and damages DNA. This helps stop dividing cancer cells but can also affect blood-cell production and reproductive tissues.
agents.watch: Use the prescribed anti-sickness and hydration plan. Report fever, painful urination or blood in the urine.

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: Cells use tiny structures called microtubules to separate their chromosomes when dividing. Paclitaxel stabilises these structures so they cannot rearrange normally, interrupting cell division. It can also affect nerves and other healthy tissues.
agents.watch: Report tingling or numbness before the next weekly dose, especially if it affects walking or hand use. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, chest or throat tightness, itching, dizziness or breathing changes during infusion.
risks: Hair loss, muscle or joint pain
Mouth, bowel, skin and nail effects

context_label: Adjuvant or neoadjuvant high-risk node-negative or node-positive breast cancer
purpose: Reduce recurrence risk as part of the agreed early-breast treatment plan.
schedule_summary: Four AC treatments (doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²) 14 days apart, followed 14 days after the last AC by 12 weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m² doses, subject to recovery. The planned sequence spans about 20 weeks.

timeline_note: Planned treatment days are distinct from broad possible symptom patterns. Symptoms can occur outside these bands.
safety_note: There are no guaranteed safe days. Fever, shivers, sudden illness, new breathing problems or severe symptoms need prompt advice on any day, including a treatment break.

urgent_extra: Report new breathlessness, jaundice, marked bleeding, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink, chest symptoms or a severe rash promptly.

support.title: Nerve symptoms

support.title: Review the plan

questions.q: Why was this treatment chosen for me?
questions.a: This anthracycline–taxane sequence is an option for selected high-risk early breast cancer. Dose-dense AC needs growth-factor support; the later weekly paclitaxel phase has different premedicines and toxicity priorities.

questions.q: What happens if a dose is delayed or missed?
questions.a: A delayed, omitted or changed dose needs an updated plan from the treating team. Do not move doses or restart on your own.

questions.q: Who arranges the checks and explains the results?
questions.a: Agree the due window, booking team, result reviewer and contact route if a test or appointment is missing. This page does not record completed checks.

questions.q: Can I take other medicines or supplements?
questions.a: Check new prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines and supplements with the oncology pharmacist before taking them.

items.title: Your treatment setting
items.text: Adjuvant or neoadjuvant high-risk node-negative or node-positive breast cancer

items.title: Your exact schedule
items.text: Four AC treatments (doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²) 14 days apart, followed 14 days after the last AC by 12 weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m² doses, subject to recovery. The planned sequence spans about 20 weeks.

items.title: Alternatives
items.text: Discuss biomarker-directed, endocrine, chemotherapy and supportive-care options appropriate to this setting, including the option not to proceed.

chapters.title: Checks across treatment
chapters.intro: Your team arranges tests and reviews the results before treatment decisions.

items.title: Blood and organ checks
items.text: FBC, kidney and liver tests at baseline and before each cycle, with the unit confirming weekly paclitaxel test requirements. Review current illness and past dose delays separately.

items.title: Other treatment-specific checks
items.text: Review lifetime anthracycline exposure and cardiac risk. Echo/MUGA is indicated above age 65 or when clinically indicated; the source requires LVEF above 50% for doxorubicin. Reassess cardiac symptoms and neuropathy as indicated; no trastuzumab is included.

items.title: Cancer review and follow-up
items.text: After early-breast treatment, breast imaging and clinical review follow the agreed plan. Routine CT/PET scans or blood tumour markers are not used to search for distant recurrence in someone without symptoms or clinical concerns.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Bone-health assessment follows endocrine therapy, ovarian suppression, menopause and other fracture risks. It has its own monitoring plan.

chapters.title: The wider treatment plan
chapters.intro: For neoadjuvant treatment, agree response review and surgery planning. After surgery, confirm radiotherapy and endocrine treatment where appropriate; their schedules and checks remain separate.

items.title: Treatment changes
items.text: A delayed, omitted or changed dose needs an updated plan from the treating team. Do not move doses or restart on your own.

items.title: Medicines review
items.text: Check new prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines and supplements with the oncology pharmacist before taking them.

items.title: After treatment
items.text: Keep the agreed follow-up and report persistent or new symptoms between visits.

phases.label: Weekly paclitaxel

logistics.intro: Four AC treatments (doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²) 14 days apart, followed 14 days after the last AC by 12 weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m² doses, subject to recovery. The planned sequence spans about 20 weeks.

steps.title: Before treatment
steps.text: FBC, kidney and liver tests at baseline and before each cycle, with the unit confirming weekly paclitaxel test requirements. Review current illness and past dose delays separately.

steps.title: Plan venous access
steps.text: A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. A port is not automatically required; insertion and removal are separate procedures with individual instructions.

steps.title: On the treatment day
steps.text: Confirm the medicines due that day, any premedicines and the reviewed blood results. Tell staff immediately about pain, burning, rash or breathlessness.

steps.title: After the visit
steps.text: No routine take-home infusion pump is required for this regimen. Keep line-care, urgent-contact and next-review instructions.

details.title: Visit length
details.text: AC and weekly paclitaxel have different visit and supportive-medicine plans. The unit confirms the complete appointment duration.

details.title: Line care
details.text: A PICC or port has its own care plan. Report fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or line damage; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: Treatment changes
details.text: A delayed, omitted or changed dose needs an updated plan from the treating team. Do not move doses or restart on your own.

details.title: Support for this visit
details.text: G-CSF is required for every dose-dense AC cycle. Prescribe product, dose and timing separately under the approved local plan. First paclitaxel dose: dexamethasone 8 mg IV, chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV, each 30 minutes before treatment (NCCP suggested table).

anatomy: Hair loss or thinning varies; ask about support.
Painful ulcers or difficulty drinking need advice.
New cough or breathlessness needs prompt assessment.
New chest pain, fainting or severe breathlessness needs urgent assessment.
Report diarrhoea early, especially with poor intake or dizziness.
Report numbness, tingling or pain affecting daily activity.
Fever, shivers, unusual bleeding or sudden illness: call promptly.
Report severe rash, blistering or yellow skin / eyes promptly.
